definitions.gloss: new construction; newly built structure or vessel
definitions.explanation: Refers to the building of something new, especially ships, buildings, or other large structures. Most commonly used in the context of shipbuilding to mean a newly constructed ship.
An older usage referring to a newly married woman or young wife. This sense is now archaic or dialectal but appears in classical literature and historical texts.

examples.japanese: {新造|しんぞう}{船|せん}が{完成|かんせい}した。
examples.english: The newly built ship was completed.

examples.japanese: この{空港|くうこう}は{新造|しんぞう}ターミナルの{建設|けんせつ}を{計画|けいかく}している。
examples.english: This airport is planning the construction of a new terminal.

examples.japanese: {海上自衛隊|かいじょうじえいたい}は{護衛艦|ごえいかん}の{新造|しんぞう}を{発注|はっちゅう}した。
examples.english: The Maritime Self-Defense Force placed an order for the construction of a new escort ship.

examples.japanese: {新造|しんぞう}さんは{美|うつく}しい{人|ひと}だった。
examples.english: The young bride was a beautiful woman.

examples.japanese: {江戸時代|えどじだい}の{小説|しょうせつ}には{新造|しんぞう}という{言葉|ことば}がよく{出|で}てくる。
examples.english: The word shinzou appears frequently in Edo-period novels.

examples.japanese: あの{遊郭|ゆうかく}の{新造|しんぞう}は{評判|ひょうばん}がよかった。
examples.english: The young woman at that pleasure quarter had a good reputation.

notes:
Primarily used in modern Japanese to refer to the construction of new ships, buildings, or large structures. The word carries a sense of building from scratch rather than renovating or modifying.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {新造|しんぞう}{船|せん}: newly built ship
- {船|ふね}の{新造|しんぞう}: construction of a new ship
- {新造|しんぞう}{費|ひ}: construction cost (for new build)
- {新造|しんぞう}{車両|しゃりょう}: newly manufactured rolling stock

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {新築|しんちく}: new construction (specifically buildings and houses)
- {建造|けんぞう}: construction (used for ships and large structures, emphasizes the building process)
- {造船|ぞうせん}: shipbuilding (the industry or activity in general)

HISTORICAL NOTE:
In Edo-period usage, {新造|しんぞう} referred to a young woman, especially a newly married wife or a young woman working in the pleasure quarters. This sense survives in historical fiction and period dramas but is not used in modern everyday speech.
